PORT 222.d: This course provides credit for students who have successfully completed approved examinations, such as Advanced Placement exams. This credit counts toward the total credit hours required for graduation. Mutually Exclusive: Cannot register for PORT 222 if student has credit for PORT 141 or PORT 106. Mutually Exclusive: Cannot register for PORT 222 if student has credit for PORT 106/PORT 141.
PORT 222.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

PORT 303.d: In this course students will develop their skills in cultural analysis using a broad range of courses such as literature, film, and other audio-visual materials. Readings as well as in-class discussions will provide the historical and cultural context necessary to critical analysis. Students will be able to advance their conversation and writing skills in Portuguese. Previously offered as SPPO 303. Mutually exclusive. Credit cannot be earned for PORT 303 if student has previously taken SPPO 303. Recommended Prerequisite(s): PORT 264
PORT 303.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

PORT 238.d: Topics and credit hours may vary each semester. Contact department for current semester’s topic(s). Repeatable for Credit.
PORT 238.type: Independent Study, Internship/Practicum, Laboratory, Lecture, Lecture/Laboratory, Seminar
PORT 238.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

PORT 302.d: The purpose of this course is to develop speaking, reading, and writing skills via the analysis of Brazilian literary and cultural texts. Through a multidisciplinary approach, students will be introduced to cultural analysis using a broad range of sources such as literature, film, and other audio-visual materials.
PORT 302.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

PORT 331.d: Course examines topics in contemporary Brazil as presented in media, literature, film, and music. Works address persistent race, class, and gender inequalities, national identity, urban life, and environmental issues, among other topics. Further development of speaking, writing and vocabulary enrichment emphasized through discussions and interactive activities. Taught in Portuguese. Recommended Prerequisite(s): PORT 302, placement test, or permission of instructor.
PORT 331.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

PORT 106.d: Alternate first-year Portuguese for students who have a good command of Spanish. This is an intensive course covering the equivalents of PORT 141 and 142. Students will be prepared for PORT 206 upon completion of the course. Placement Test is required. Effective May 15, 2019, this course does not carry D1 credit. Mutually Exclusive: Cannot register for PORT 106 if student has credit for PORT 142/PORT 222.
PORT 106.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

PORT 321.d: This course is part of the Rice in Brazil program. It focuses on developing advanced conversational competence in Portuguese through immersive experiences in Brazil. To develop the skills necessary to be competent conversationalists, students will analyze authentic and semi-authentic conversations. The course emphasizes practical conversational aspects by providing hands-on experience with both formal and informal language in diverse contexts. By the end, students will confidently engage in culturally and contextually appropriate conversations, demonstrating a nuanced understanding of pragmatics, societal norms, and cultural subtleties in Brazil. This course is part of the Rice in Country program and is not eligible for audit.
PORT 321.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

PORT 477.d: Topics and credit hours may vary each semester. Contact department for current semester's topic(s). Repeatable for Credit.
PORT 477.type: Internship/Practicum, Laboratory, Lecture, Lecture/Laboratory, Seminar, Independent Study
PORT 477.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

PORT 301.d: Continuation of PORT 206. Emphasis on further developing interactional and intercultural competence in Portuguese as more authentic materials and socio-cultural topics are covered.
PORT 301.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

PORT 206.d: Intermediate Portuguese for students who have a very good command of Spanish. This accelerated course covers the equivalent of two semesters of Portuguese. It will focus on developing interactional and intercultural competence in Portuguese to communicate appropriately with Portuguese speakers. Students will also be introduced to the sociocultural aspects of Brazil. Mutually Exclusive: Cannot register for PORT 206 if student has credit for PORT 263/PORT 264.
PORT 206.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.
